# Setup
```{r, message=FALSE}
# knitr options
knitr::opts_chunk$set(dpi = 300, collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", error = TRUE)

# packages 
library(here)
library(tidyverse)
library(bioseq)

# here setup
basedir <- here("species/crob/KH13")
```

# Background

Goals:

1. Ghost database (KH13) has two protein fasta files; one for the longest ORF where all proteins don't start with methionine, and one where amino acids before the first methionine have been removed so all proteins start with a methionine. We try to figure out whether to use the former or the latter with eggnog-mapper. 
2. The KH13 protein fasta files have invalid characters. How do we deal with them?

# Longest ORF vs starting with methionine

We can look at, as reference, whether amphioxus protein fasta files from NCBI have proteins that start with methionine. 

```{r}
bf_proteins <- read_fasta(here("species/bflo/genome/refseq__GCF_000003815.2_Bfl_VNyyK/GCF_000003815.2_Bfl_VNyyK/GCF_000003815.2_Bfl_VNyyK_protein.faa"), type = "AA") %>% 
  as_tibble.bioseq_aa()
```

Distribution of first amino acids for amphioxus
```{r}
bf_proteins %>% 
  mutate(first_aa = str_extract(sequence, "^.")) %>% 
  count(first_aa) %>% 
  arrange(-n)
```

We can see that 42,919 of 43,041 amphioxus proteins in the fasta file start with a methionine. 

## Solution
We will use the file for Ciona where the proteins start with a methionine. 

# Invalid characters in the fasta file

I tried running eggnogmapper using the `KH.KHGene.2013.Longest.protein.fasta` and `KH.KHGene.2013.Met.protein.fasta` files, but both jobs failed. The error was:

```
Error running diamond: Error: Error reading input stream at line 354: Invalid character (+) in sequence
```

This was for the Met fasta; the line number for the first file was different. But essentially, **there are non-standard characters in the amino acid fasta**, specifically, at least `+` character in some places. 

Here, we try to figure out if we can replace the non-standard characters with something that won't result in an error with eggnog-mapper. 

## Examine the fasta file read with `{bioseq}`

```{r}
longest <- read_fasta(here(basedir, "data/ghost-db/KH.KHGene.2013.Longest.protein.fasta"), type = "AA") %>% 
  as_tibble.bioseq_aa()

met <- read_fasta(here(basedir, "data/ghost-db/KH.KHGene.2013.Met.protein.fasta"), type = "AA") %>% 
  as_tibble.bioseq_aa()
```

We can see here that `bioseq::read_fasta()` also complains about the non-standard characters in the fasta file. 

### Aside about N and X

The warning message says that these characters have been replaced with "N". N is supposed to be aspargine. N is supposed to mean "any character" in nucleotide sequences but not in protein sequences; for protein sequences the "any character" placeholder is "X" (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FASTA_format).

```
Warning message:
Non-standard IUPAC symbols detected for AA: 1357 characters were converted to N.
```

If we look at the code for `bioseq::new_aa()` (https://github.com/fkeck/bioseq/blob/f8adcc1895dfbda5b5170fda413786ecc9458743/R/def_aa.R#L9-L16) (`read_fasta()` uses `aa()` which in turn uses `new_aa()`), we can see that invalid characters are in fact replaced by X (as they should be) and not by N. 

```
new_aa <- function(x = character()) {
  vec_assert(x, character())
  x <- validate_seq(x,
                    alphabet = dic_aa()$alphabet,
                    invalid_replacement = "X",
                    type = "AA")
  new_vctr(x, class = "bioseq_aa")
}
```

It's only the warning message where N is printed regardless of the type "DNA" or "AA", as we can see in the code for `validate_seq()` (https://github.com/fkeck/bioseq/blob/f8adcc1895dfbda5b5170fda413786ecc9458743/R/checks_validation.R#L27-L47). I should point this out to the author of `{bioseq}`. 
```
validate_seq <- function(x, alphabet, invalid_replacement, type = "DNA") {
  stopifnot(is.character(x))
  x_names <- names(x)
  x <- gsub("([abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz])","\\U\\1", x, perl = TRUE)
  x <- stringr::str_replace_all(x, pattern = "\\.", replacement = "-")
  x <- stringr::str_replace_all(x, pattern = "[:blank:]|\n", replacement = "")
  rgx_nonvalid <- paste0("[^", paste(alphabet, collapse = ""), "]")
  n_nonvalid <- sum(stringr::str_count(x, pattern = rgx_nonvalid),
                    na.rm = TRUE)
  if(n_nonvalid > 0) {
    x <- stringr::str_replace_all(x, pattern = rgx_nonvalid,
                                  replacement = invalid_replacement)
    warning("Non-standard IUPAC symbols detected for ",
            type,": ", n_nonvalid,
            " characters were converted to N.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  if(!is.null(x_names)){
    names(x) <- x_names
  }
  return(x)
}
```
## Solution for non-standard characters

I think, we can simply read in the fasta files with bioseq, let bioseq replace the non-standard characters with `X`, write them to fasta files, and use those files for eggnog-mapper. 

## Sanity check 

Even though we already have a solution, I want to make sure independently that we are in fact replacing the right characters. For this, we will read the fasta files with `read_lines()` and compare them with the `bioseq`-read versions. 

```{r}
lines_to_fasta <- function(x) {
  x %>% 
    split(cumsum(grepl("^>", .))) %>% # split by sequence name 
    set_names(map_chr(., ~ .x[1])) %>%  # use first line as seq name
    map(~ tail(.x, -1)) %>% # remove the first line (seq name)
    map(~ paste0(.x, collapse = "")) %>% # multiline seq to single line seq
    enframe(name = "name", value = "seq") %>% # list to data frame
    mutate(seq = unlist(seq)) %>% 
    mutate(name = str_remove(name, "^>")) # remove > from seq names
}
```


```{r}
longest2 <- read_lines(here(basedir, "data/ghost-db/KH.KHGene.2013.Longest.protein.fasta")) %>% 
  lines_to_fasta()

met2 <- read_lines(here(basedir, "data/ghost-db/KH.KHGene.2013.Met.protein.fasta")) %>% 
  lines_to_fasta()
```

```{r}
met2 %>% 
  filter(str_detect(seq, "[^A-z]")) %>% 
  mutate(len = nchar(seq)) %>% 
  arrange(len) %>% 
  print(n = 20)
```

We see that the `+` character appears mostly at the end of the sequence for some 1135 proteins. Below we see that the same proteins have an `X` at the end in the file read by `bioseq`, suggesting that `bioseq` has correctly replaced the non-standard characters. 

```{r}
met %>% 
  filter(label %in% (met2 %>% 
                       filter(str_detect(seq, "[^A-z]")) %>% 
                       pull(name))) %>% 
  mutate(len = nchar(sequence)) %>% 
  arrange(len) %>% 
  print(n = 20)
```

## Write the fixed the fasta file

NOTE: There are over a thousand 0-length proteins which cause problems with `write_fasta`. We have to get rid of them before writing the fasta file.

```{r}
fixed_fasta <- read_fasta(here(basedir,
                               "data/ghost-db/KH.KHGene.2013.Met.protein.fasta"), 
                          type = "AA")

fixed_fasta <- fixed_fasta[str_length(fixed_fasta) != 0]

write_fasta(
  fixed_fasta, 
  here(basedir, "results/fasta/KH.KHGene.2013.Met.protein_valid-chars.fasta")
)
```
